wa_colchuck_balanced_rock_west_face.primary: Lake outlet climbers' path into the west cirque

why.Southern line via the Aasgard-side slope: When the lake outlet crossing looks unreasonable; it avoids the ford but means a brushy bushwhack and a gully that can hold snow into early summer, so it takes longer.

why.Colchuck Lake, bare-ice glacier (late se: Late summer, when the glacier has melted to hard ice; needs crampons, often two tools, and a down-climb because the snow glissade is gone, so most parties prefer the early window.

wa_concord_tower_north_face.primary: Blue Lake Trail to the Liberty Bell-Concord notch

why.Early-season snow to the notch: Early in the season, once the highway reopens and before the gully melts out; it needs an axe and perhaps crampons, but the rock stays frozen in place and rockfall is lower.

wa_copper_peak_south_route.primary: Holden Village and the Copper Creek boot trail to the Copper Basin bench

why.Phelps Creek over Spider Gap: When the Lake Chelan ferry and Holden shuttle are not running; far longer, with a steep snow climb to Spider Gap, so it suits strong parties who can commit to a multi-day trip.

wa_crater_mountain_standard_route.primary: Canyon Creek trailhead, Jackita Ridge #738 and the Crater Lake trail #746

why.Devils Dome loop from the East Bank trai: When the Canyon Creek ford looks too risky, as in spring or early summer; it trades the day trip for a roughly 48-mile, three-day loop over Devils Dome.

wa_crooked_thumb_peak_south_route.primary: Hannegan Pass, the Chilliwack cable car and Whatcom Pass to Perfect Pass, then over the Challenger Glacier and through West Challenger Notch

why.Big Beaver valley and Wiley Ridge: When avoiding the Hannegan route's cable-car crossing and the long loss and regain of height near Whatcom Pass; a boat ride and an easy trail lead to a steep Wiley Ridge bushwhack, over several days.

wa_dark_peak_dark_glacier_route.primary: Swamp Creek climbers' path to the col

why.Crest trail to Hemlock Camp and the nort: To skip the thick Swamp Creek brush on easier forest slopes, though recent beetle deadfall at the old camp and on the climb to the col slows the steep start and makes it less attractive.

wa_direct_north_buttress.primary: Hannegan Pass and the Chilliwack River Trail to Bear Creek

why.From the Chilliwack Lake road on the Can: For parties already in Canada, as it is a much shorter walk to the saddle camp, but it crosses the border on foot away from a port of entry and is not a lawful way in for everyone.

wa_dome_peak_dome_glacier.primary: Downey Creek Trail #768 and the Bachelor Creek route

why.Ptarmigan Traverse from Cascade Pass: When Dome is reached as part of the whole Ptarmigan Traverse, camping at White Rock Lakes; it is much longer and needs glacier skills, so it is not chosen for Dome alone.

wa_earl_peak_southwest_ridge.primary: Bean Creek Trail to Earl Pass

why.Standup Creek trail: For a quieter, gentler start from the Standup Creek side, or when making a loop that crosses the ridge between the two creeks, with the hard climbing saved for the upper slopes.

wa_east_face.primary: Downey Creek, Bachelor Creek and Itswoot Ridge

why.From Stehekin up Agnes and Spruce Creeks: When coming from Stehekin by boat or floatplane, or linking with Dome and the Gunsights; a long trail then brush to the Icy-Spruce col, instead of the Downey Creek approach.

wa_east_ridge_2.primary: The Kindy Creek roadbed and the ribbon-marked climbers' trail to the Point 5116 saddle

why.Camping at the lake below the ridge: When splitting the climb over two days, with a comfortable camp and reliable water in the lake meadows below the ridge.
